rejected.title: Nominalisation
card: Nominalisation turns a verb or an adjective into a noun. The verb decide becomes the noun decision. The adjective safe becomes the noun safety.
A sentence with a verb often names who did the action: The council decided to close the pool. Nominalising gives: The decision to close the pool was made.
The nominalised version can leave out the person who acted. This makes the writing sound less personal.
Nominalisation also packs more information into a noun group. This makes writing sound more formal, so it is common in reports and textbooks.
rejected.remember: Turn an action or quality into a noun, and writing can sound more formal and less personal.

a.q: Which word is a nominalisation of the verb "discover"?
opts: Discovery
Discovered
Discovers
Discoverable
a.why: Discovery is a noun made from the verb discover. Discovered and discovers are still verb forms, and discoverable is an adjective, so none of them is a noun.
a.clue: Look for the noun, the word that names a thing or idea.
